state.objective: Determine whether the proposed Indonesian retail COA should be compressed further, and distinguish approved core accounts from temporary migration holds.
state.organization: One PT Perorangan. HO and retail units are sites of the same legal entity. Finance and all bank operations are centralized at HO. Units handle physical cash, petty cash, cashier float, sales cash and stock evidence but cannot operate bank accounts, post unrestricted manual journals or transact unit-to-unit.
state.posting_model: Business documents and subledgers generate postings. site_id, bank_account_id, supplier_id, employee/person_id, asset_id/class, inventory class, tender/acquirer, tax code, advance purpose and document references are dimensions or subledger attributes rather than account-code segments.

review_history.meaning: The 225 working list equals 121 designed core accounts plus 104 legacy accounts held separately pending evidence. The 142 target groups the unresolved legacy accounts into 21 possible target groups, but those merges are not authorized until evidence is obtained.

representative_core_accounts: Aset tetap by class, accumulated depreciation by class, and depreciation expense by class
Thirteen payroll nature accounts including salary, overtime, meal, transport, health, BPJS, THR, uniforms, recreation, funeral contribution, training, severance and bonus
Thirty-nine operating expense nature accounts including promotion, advertising, utilities, travel, permits, IT, supplies, maintenance, insurance and taxes
decision_principles: Keep separate natural accounts when recognition, measurement, presentation, tax, control, reconciliation or statutory disclosure differs.
Use dimensions only for identity, site, bank, party, asset, document, project, channel, purpose or operational analysis.
Do not merge debit and contra/allowance accounts merely to reduce count.
Do not force compression without evidence from balances, contracts, schedules, tax filings, asset registers and reconciliations.
A smaller account count has value only if forms and reporting become simpler without moving accounting policy into uncontrolled free-text dimensions.

approve_121_architecture.instructions: Is the 121-account core architecture a reasonable controlled production baseline for this retail company?

criteria.yes: The size and separation are proportionate to the entity and supported by subledgers/dimensions.
criteria.no_too_large: It is materially over-segmented and should be compressed before use.
criteria.no_too_small: It is too compressed for reliable accounting.

approve_225_as_permanent.instructions: Should all 225 working accounts be treated as the permanent final COA?

criteria.no_working: No; 104 are temporary evidence holds and should not be presented as approved permanent design.
criteria.remove_now: No; delete the 104 immediately without evidence.

approve_142_now.instructions: Can the 142-account conditional target be implemented immediately as final?

criteria.no_evidence: No; unresolved groups require evidence and migration mapping first.
criteria.never: No; none of the proposed merges should ever occur.

further_compression_default.instructions: What should be the default stance toward compressing the 121 core further?

criteria.stop_unless_evidence: Stop by default; merge only when a specific pair has identical accounting treatment, controls and reporting needs.
criteria.expand: Split the core into more site/bank/vendor-specific accounts.

target_around_30.instructions: Would a target near 30 natural accounts be appropriate for this company?

criteria.no: It would likely mix materially different recognition, contra, liability, tax, asset and expense natures.
criteria.yes: Thirty accounts can safely cover all stated requirements.
criteria.only_management: It may be a management-report presentation layer, not the posting COA.

benefit_of_more_reduction.instructions: Is further account-count reduction itself likely to create material operational benefit after forms no longer expose the full COA?

criteria.limited: Benefit is limited; form simplicity comes mainly from business-event forms, posting rules and search, not from forcing fewer natural accounts.
criteria.high: Every additional merge materially improves user experience.

cash_three.instructions: Should Cash on Hand, Petty Cash and Modal Kasir remain separate natural accounts?

criteria.separate: Yes; custody, purpose, replenishment and control differ even though site is a dimension.
criteria.merge: Merge into one physical cash account with cash-purpose dimension.

bank_types.instructions: Should Giro, Tabungan and Deposito remain separate account natures?

criteria.separate: Yes; liquidity, term/restriction and reconciliation treatment can differ; bank identity remains a dimension.
criteria.merge: Merge all into one Bank account.

ap_merch_nonmerch.instructions: Should merchandise AP and non-merchandise AP remain separate?

criteria.separate: Yes; purchasing flows, receipt evidence, aging and controls differ.
criteria.merge: Use one trade payable account and supplier/invoice dimensions.

grni_separate.instructions: Should GRNI remain separate from invoiced accounts payable?

criteria.separate: Yes; it represents received-uninvoiced accrual requiring PO-GRN-invoice matching.

advances_three.instructions: Should supplier, employee/travel and other advances remain separate natural accounts?

criteria.separate: Yes; party, settlement, tax and control workflows differ.
criteria.merge: Use one Advances account with purpose and party dimensions.

prepaid_rent_general.instructions: Should prepaid rent remain separate from general prepaid expenses?

criteria.separate: Yes; leases/rent commonly have distinct schedules, periods and disclosure/tax considerations.
criteria.merge: Use one prepaid account with schedule type.

ar_classes.instructions: Should acquirer receivables remain separate from employee/management receivables?

criteria.separate: Yes; settlement source, credit risk, aging and controls differ.
criteria.merge: Use one receivable account with party type.

allowances.instructions: Should receivable and inventory allowances remain separate from gross assets and from each other?

criteria.separate: Yes; they are contra accounts with different measurement and reconciliation bases.
criteria.merge_gross: Net them directly into gross assets.
criteria.one_allowance: Use one allowance account for all assets.

inventory_merch_bags.instructions: Should merchandise inventory and shopping-bag inventory remain separate?

criteria.separate: Yes; merchandise and consumable/package inventory have different operational and costing behavior.
criteria.merge: Use one inventory account with item class.

inventory_transit.instructions: Should in-transit inventory remain separate from on-hand inventory?

criteria.separate: Yes; custody and receipt status require distinct reconciliation.

fixed_asset_triplets.instructions: Should fixed-asset cost, accumulated depreciation and depreciation expense remain separate account families?

criteria.separate: Yes; gross cost, contra asset and expense cannot be merged.
criteria.merge: Use one account per asset class for all three.

asset_classes.instructions: Can all fixed-asset classes be compressed into a single fixed-asset cost account plus one accumulated depreciation and one expense account?

criteria.keep_classes: Keep meaningful classes where useful life, tax, disclosure or control differs; asset_id handles identity.
criteria.single_class: Use only three natural accounts for every fixed asset.
criteria.more_classes: Split every physical item into its own GL account.

accrual_types.instructions: Should employee, interest, rent and utilities accruals remain separate?

criteria.separate: Yes; reversals, counterparties, estimates and reporting differ.
criteria.merge: Use one accrued expenses account with accrual_type dimension.

tax_five.instructions: Should the five tax asset/liability accounts remain separated at this level?

criteria.separate: Yes; input VAT, income-tax credits, PBB/other prepaid tax and tax payable have distinct return/reconciliation treatment.
criteria.merge: Use one tax control account and tax code dimension.

revenue_natures.instructions: Should merchandise sales, rental, management fee, interest and other income remain separate?

criteria.separate: Yes; operating nature, presentation, tax and source subledger differ.
criteria.merge: Use one Revenue account with revenue_type dimension.

contra_revenue.instructions: Should sales returns and discounts remain separate from gross sales?

criteria.separate: Yes; preserve gross-to-net reporting and controls.

payroll_thirteen.instructions: Should all 13 payroll expense accounts remain separate?

criteria.review_subset: Retain statutory/materially distinct items, but evidence may support merging minor benefits into broader employee-benefit groups.
criteria.keep_all: Every one of 13 must remain permanently separate.
criteria.one_payroll: Merge all into one Payroll expense account.

opex_thirtynine.instructions: What is the appropriate treatment of the 39 operating-expense accounts?

criteria.selective_review: Review low-volume accounts using materiality, tax, budget ownership and recurring management reporting; merge only demonstrably homogeneous natures.
criteria.one_opex: Merge all into one Operating expense account.

expense_dimension_boundary.instructions: When is an expense distinction better modeled as a dimension rather than a natural account?

criteria.identity_or_purpose: When the difference is site, department, project, vendor, campaign, vehicle, device or specific item identity while recognition and reporting nature are the same.
criteria.always_dimension: Every expense distinction should be a dimension.
criteria.never_dimension: Every operational distinction needs a GL account.

payroll_possible_reduction.instructions: Is payroll the most plausible core domain for modest additional compression?

criteria.yes_evidence: Yes, especially minor employee benefits if payroll/tax/reporting treatment is identical, but only after evidence review.
criteria.no: No payroll accounts can ever merge.
criteria.all: All payroll expenses should become one account now.

opex_possible_reduction.instructions: Is operating expense the most plausible core domain for modest additional compression?

criteria.yes_evidence: Yes; low-volume homogeneous expenses may merge after materiality, tax and budget-report review.
criteria.no: No OPEX accounts can ever merge.
criteria.all: All OPEX should become one account now.

asset_possible_reduction.instructions: Is fixed-asset class compression safe without reviewing useful lives, tax classes and the asset register?

criteria.no: No; require register and policy evidence before merging classes.

stop_rule.instructions: What stopping rule should govern further COA compression?

criteria.evidence_and_value: Stop when remaining distinctions affect accounting/control/reporting, or when further merging adds no meaningful form/search benefit; require evidence for every proposed merge.
criteria.numeric_target: Continue until a predetermined account count is reached regardless of evidence.

recommended_next_action.instructions: What should the project do next?

criteria.implement_core_review_holds: Implement the 121-account core and dimensions, keep 104 holds migration-only, then resolve them with balances/schedules/contracts/registers; separately review payroll and OPEX for modest evidence-based reduction.
criteria.compress_first: Delay implementation until the entire COA reaches 30-50 accounts.
criteria.implement_225_permanent: Make all 225 permanent and end review.
